Marine Metal Aeratr Bubble Box 1.5V Reviewing the comments first I see one person says he used it twice and it worked both times. Then he gave it three stars because he said it might break sometime. Well.

With nearly 5k reviews what more can be said? Me personal? I like using the shipping container to protect the device. It has the holes in the right places and the batteries load from the front so there is no muss or fuss. Stick it back in the plastic once and you're good to go.

I keep my fishing minners in an old round 2 gallon or so water dispenser. You've seen them. Construction guys use them and campers. This time I never lost a single minnow all day. That is a FIRST. I drilled a tube size hole near the top and duct taped a string on top. Used the handy clamp to hold the unit in place. Like I said, worked great...not too noisy. I like it. Fine!

text_fidelity_a:
NCAA Missouri Tigers Can Cooler, 16 I am a Pittsburgh Steelers fan, so I admit that I just picked this cooler for the colors, and I don't even know the Missouri Tigers. But cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it!

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can put things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

I could have picked any of the NCAA teams that they make this cooler for, but I happened to pick the colors of my favorite pro football team, the Pittsburgh Steelers. (OK, I'm frugal and couldn't spring for the much more expensive Steelers cooler, but this way I get my team colors AND an awesome cooler.)
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Missouri Tigers Can Cooler, 16

text_fidelity_a:
Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black If you have the type of seat post where the saddle rails are sandwiched/clamped between two contoured plates this saddle might not work on your seat post clamp. This saddle comes with one of those rotary, rotating, claw-type clamps and the saddle likely works fine with that included clamp. However better bike seat posts can't use the included claw clamp type -- they must use their own sandwich-type. Technically, this saddle still should still mount but the distance between the rails was too wide. If you are confused about the difference do a web search for 'bike seat rail clamp' and you'll see the two different families of clamps.

I would have thought that the measured distance between saddle rails would be standardized but the rails on this saddle were just a very few millimeters too wide for both my sandwich-type clamps (it failed to mount on the two different seat post clamps I tried it on). The distance could maybe be lessened by clamping the rails, in a vice, for example, or using some other tool but I decided to return it rather than mess with it..

Otherwise it seemed okay, maybe quite a bit on the stiff side for a gel saddle.
text_fidelity_b: Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black

text_fidelity_a:
FORM Smart Swim Goggles with Free 1-Year Membership, Fitness Tracker with a See-Through Display That Shows Your Metrics While Swimming UPDATE: I decided against renewing my membership (although FORM went ahead and did and I had to fire off an email telling I didn't want to! Aren't companies supposed to notify you before auto-renewing???). I wasn't using the pre-fab workouts, I couldn't care less about following anyone or having anyone follow me (honestly, does EVERYTHING need to be "social"? No, it does not!) . ONE feature, and I mean the ONE feature I used and only for the 6 months of my year long subscription that it was FINALLY available was the Custom Workouts that allowed me to create my own workouts. I have a triathlon coach who writes my workouts and then I would re-create them in the app, then sync with the goggles. It worked great until I ended my subscription ended. Now, it doesn't work at all. They want me to pay $15/month for the privileged of creating MY OWN WORKOUTS???? Nope! I am updating my warning. They have terrible customer service. The goggles fog up and leak. They're uncomfortable. The app is pretty useless. And SOOOOOO not worth the price or the subscription. They're junk.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I bought them directly from FORM. I'm reviewing here to warn others!

I'll start with the positive: I get a lap split and stroke count that I can see every 25. That's it. That's the only good thing I can say.

They leak, despite trying EVERY nose bridge piece. Customer service strung me along telling me to try different things until it was too late to return for a refund. The app is worthless to me. I don't need canned workouts. I have a coach that writes my workouts. Workouts I can't re-create or import in the Form app. The final blow was after a software update notification, I was not able to update them nor use them at all! They bricked! I've only used them twice a week for 3 months! After a week of repeating the same trouble-shooting steps over and over again, they are sending me a new pair. Not what I wanted. I would have preferred a refund! I wouldn't GIVE these to my worst enemy, let alone recommend them. Take my advice: Don't buy them.
text_fidelity_b: FORM Smart Swim Goggles with Free 1-Year Membership, Fitness Tracker with a See-Through Display That Shows Your Metrics While Swimming

text_fidelity_a: Sunny Health & Fitness Mini Stepper Stair Stepper Exercise Equipment with Resistance Bands This compact stepper is perfect for small spaces.. like a 1 bedroom apartment, studio, or your office!  In my included photo, I place the machine next to my personal paper shredder so that you can see that it's not that big.  The machine came already assembled.  The only thing that I had to do was pull the safety tab from the battery compartment of the digital display, put the display in its designated spot on the machine, attached the resistance bands, and adjust the step height.  Instructions are super simple to follow and the machine itself is easy to use.  You should find an extra battery for the display in the box as well which was great of them to include.  The machine weighs about 14.2 lbs, so I can easily move it around.  I love that it has a display which will tell you the number of steps, the length of time that the steps are done in, and how many calories have been burned.  The display powers on either when the red button on the display is pushed or when the steps are put in motion, and it will auto shut off after not being used for 4 minutes.  You can easily pick up where you left off by powering on the display, and it retains the info until you reset it.  Resetting the display is easy - just press the red button for a few seconds until the display resets.  The instructions do advise you to place an exercise mat under the machine to protect your floors.  I use this machine every day while I watch TV, and I can see toning in my lower abdomen, thighs, and bottom from it.  I do have to admit that I don't use the resistance bands very often, so I just lay those to the side and do the steps, but I do like that I have the option to use them.  I am NOT an exercise enthusiast - I'm getting older & was advised to be active at least 30 minutes/day, so this was an easy solution for me.  The ONLY improvement that I would make to this machine is having a lighted display.  I have a hard time seeing the display while I'm using the machine because it's somewhat dark.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Mini Stepper Stair Stepper Exercise Equipment with Resistance Bands

Obviously this treadmill is a lemon and they should have just replaced it after several "attempts" to fix it. On the other hand, if you read their "warranty" (yes, I put that in quotes on purpose), it says if they replace equipment, you no longer have a warranty. It can also be used to tie things up, as a tourniquet, or to string up an emergency shelter. The thing that sets these bracelets apart is that it is adjustable and has a toggle button on it so it can be tightened and secured even around a smaller sized wrist so it can't be easily lost. The one disappointment about these bracelets is that they did not come with instructions, so although the product description on Amazon says it comes with a flint magnesium fire starter, we weren't exactly sure where that was on the bracelet or how to use it, so directions would have been helpful. text_fidelity_a:
Camelbak Podium Chill Bottle While this can seem like an instance of someone inventing a better mouse trap, the valve on this bottle really is frustration free compared to typical bike bottles.

The valve is essentially open all of the time, but water will only come out if you squeeze it -- not so easy that it will come out when handling it, such as removing it from the bottle holder, but still not requiring much force. So you never get into instances when you're using your teeth to open the valve, sucking on the bottle or putting a death grip on it just to get the water out.

As for its insulation abilities, reviewers are grossly overstating just how cool it will keep liquids. There simply isn't much insulation -- and not room for much -- so on a sunny summer day the ice will still melt pretty fast. Don't expect that it will keep your liquids ice cold for much more than an hour after filling it up.
text_fidelity_b: Camelbak Podium Chill Bottle

text_fidelity_a:
ust Freestyle Lightweight Sleeping air mat with Ultra Light Design, Pump Sack and Carry case for Backpacking, bikepacking, yakpacking, Camping and Hiking This mat, inflated, measures 6 feet in length and 19.5 inches in width at its widest point, and about 2 inches thick. That’s definitely a minimal mat. Packed and not in the bag, the mat measures about 4 inches in diameter and 9 inches in length. On the R-rating line on the included card, it says “R value *: 2 (*visit UST site). When I visited the site, someone had asked in the Q&A about the R value. The answer from “juanito”, who I assume is with the company, was as follows: “We’re in the process of finalizing testing on the R-value right now. The freestyle will be near R:2 based on the design and our internal testing. The freestyle is not insulated, so it’s not overly warm. It’s mostly designed to be lightweight and packable.” I would agree. Don’t use it in cool/cold weather and expect it to provide any ground insulation on its own. While the included specification card lists it as weighing 17 oz, I put it on a scale and it weighs 21 oz packed with the included stuff sack/ inflation pump. The stuff sack / pump design is, I believe, basically a copy of a more well-known manufacturer’s design, which is probably patented, hence it’s not an exact copy. The stuff sack is a medium size, and will hold other things inside other than just the mat. Quality, on a scale of 1-10 would probably be a 6 or 7. The 7 inch nozzle that is used to attach the pump to the mat leaves something to be desired, but overall the pump worked ok, not great. But it did do the job, inflating in probably about 6 full pumps. While this mat does not have a dedicated air release hole, surprisingly, it wasn’t that difficult to get the air released, as the “passive” one-way valve in the air hole released the air pretty well and folding up was relatively easy. Overall, this would be a decent mat for a small, lightweight person, intending for use in warm weather.

At over a hundred bucks. . . It’s crazy expensive for a Made in China mat.
text_fidelity_b: ust Freestyle Lightweight Sleeping air mat with Ultra Light Design, Pump Sack and Carry case for Backpacking, bikepacking, yakpacking, Camping and Hiking

The DoublePlus Fan for Peloton arrived in a nice, plain black box, perfect for gifting if you choose. It would also make a good place to store the instructions, cord, and/or fan if you wanted to. The clamp is wide enough to go on our handle bars, but could also mount on something like a desk or shelf, the grip strips holding it in place and enough variance of width for a few different sizes. I'd be careful not to overdo, but it should hold up to decent pressure. We have not - yet - had to charge, but it should be easy, based on what we're seeing. I'll update if anything changes in the coming months, but as of this writing, I'm comfortable, and this little DoublePlus Fan for Peloton has been a great find!

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine We took delivery three weeks ago. Relatively easy to set up, but be aware that the seat likes to slide to the end of the stops. Now that we are used to it, my wife and I use it every day, sometimes multiple times a day. We don't put it away, just leave it in place next to the wall, facing the TV.
My main issue is that it, like all the other rowers I've seen, sits too low for someone who (like me) is 76 and 250lbs, with bad knees. At first, I'd either fall the last three inches, hopefully onto the seat, or need some sort of support to get on and off. I solved that problem by wrapping an old belt around the body (see pic), which I could use as a grab bar to lower myself on and lift myself off. If Sunny would put a grab handle on the front, that would be a big help, and save on belts.
A secondary issue is the LCD display. Others have complained that it's not bright enough. The real problem is that it's at the wrong angle. I repurposed a chunk of plastic foam packing to lift the bottom enough to make it clearly visible when seated. Sunny could duplicate that with a simple folding frame.
I should also note that the labeling on the display is wrong. Label says: Time, Count, Total Count, Calories. Actual is: Time, Count, Calories, Total Count.
Finally, I note that almost all of the self-help videos on rowing emphasize managing your strokes per minute. The display doesn't show that. I'd be willing to give up both Total Count and Calories to get that in the display. After all, Total Count is only useful if you are the only person using the machine, and Calories are pretty much a meaningless guess without information like body weight.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine

If I want to draw/write/read, I'd have a place to sit. As much as I love nature, I don't want to sit on the ground with the little creatures that will bite me. We have some smaller stools that my children use for marshmallow roasting, but they're too small for me. Since this one is considered XL, I thought it might be a better fit for me. It's not. It's still small. While it's slightly bigger than my children's other ones, it's not by much. My children have even complained about how uncomfortable this one is. I had decided to have it around for a reading chair(so my children could bring it wherever I'm doing chores or sitting and read to me), but two of them have already fallen out of it(it slipped beneath them). The first time was when one of my children was laughing at a book and I joked with him that he was laughing so hard, he fell out of his chair. One of my other children fell, too, though, after that. I think it won't be a big deal if it's on the ground or carpet, but on a flatter surface, like hardwood floor, it slips out from under a smaller person(at least), easily. Overall, with this one being considered an XL stool, we've been disappointed with it, but it does still provide a lightweight sitting option for when needed.

text_fidelity_a:
Topeak Explorer Rack I will first say the build quality of the rack seems good, and if you can get it mounted correctly to your specific bike, it will likely be a good rack for you.

However the rack could have been designed to fit more bikes better with a little more forethought. The product description says this rack is 16 x 14.5 x 9 inches. Maybe it is, however the critical dimension is the length of the support post for tire clearance reasons. The distance from the center of the bolt hole on the bottom, to the bent bar on top - ie the clearance measurement - is 14 and 15/16 inches. A 29er tire radius is obviously 14.5 inches, so if you were to mount the bottom of this level with your axle bolt you would have only 7/16 inch clearance - less than half an inch. Most rack mounting holes are well above the axle point, but some are not much. I was using P-clips since my frame has not rack holes, and even though I was completely free to mount wherever I wanted, I had trouble finding a usable position with much clearance. Since most 29ers are used in the mud at least on occasion, a little more clearance would have been nice.

Secondly, the hardware included is stainless M5 x 0.8, and there are just enough assuming your frame has the proper mounting holes. If your using P-clips or any other method, a trip to the hardware store will be required, and you likely won't find stainless hardware in metric. It wouldn't have killed them to add an extra bag of hardware for other bike mounting methods.

Lastly, if you plan to use the Topeak accessories for mounting then the top of the rack will be great for you. If your not, the top of the rack is not flat like most racks (because of the MTX grooves for easy accessory mounting). If your not using topeak bags and such, you should still be able to make it work fine, its just not flat.

Unfortunately there aren't many racks out there yet for 29ers, so this still might be a good fit for many.
text_fidelity_b: Topeak Explorer Rack

Burley Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer I like it ok, overall. I've never used a trailer before so it takes some getting used to in how the weight pulls on the bike, etc. I put three twelve-packs of Coke on it and pulled it around the neighborhood. Up hills, down hills, on sidewalks and all. Pulls good. Folds up nicely and I like the bag and straps that come with it. Seems easy to pull up stairs if you need to. Hitch for bike is nice and easy to use. But there are a few "issues".

For an item made in China, it's very expensive. The design could have been a lot better to allow you to also carry things in it like groceries. Instead, they offer a separate, very expensive, "shopping bag" as a separate option/purchase.

I honestly don't know of anyone who rides their bike to work with a large suitcase, kind of like what is shown on the video. If you're traveling with your suitcase, then you're probably going to the airport, and not on your bike. On the other hand, I think it would work well for golf clubs if you were going to play a round somewhere. Pulling it through an aisle at a grocery store, or pulling it through Wal-Mart is just crazy. If it had "wings" that folded-open to form the sides, and then a "mesh" on the front . . . then I think it would have a lot more versatility.

In the end, I just don't know how useful it is for most people, especially for the price. If you're looking for something more affordable, simply to carry things around, you might try the Aosom Bicycle Bike Cargo Trailer.

text_fidelity_a:
Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel I bought two of these and both were non-functional, out of the box.

On the first one, the included line was tangled around inside the mechanism. I had to take it apart and unravel about 6 feet of line that was all caught up in the case. It's hard to explain, but it was basically wedged between the outer casing and the internal components, not just in the spool itself.

On the second one, the casting button was completely unseated on one side. The button has two small pegs which pivot inside of holes in the steel case. I had to take the bottom of the case off, bend the steel tabs that hold the pegs in place, reseat the button and bend the tabs back.

Both work great now and all the components seem pretty good, but this company has some serious quality control issues with assembly. It is pretty ridiculous that 2 out of 2 that I ordered were DOA, still sealed in the undamaged factory box. Luckily, I knew how to fix them, but most people who aren't mechanically inclined or perhaps know very little about reels would have had to return both of them. That is really unacceptable.

Still, they are great little reels now and they would be 5 star if not for the time I had to spend on fixing them. If you have some tools and are confident about taking things apart, I wouldn't hesitate to buy one. If not, well, you might be rolling the dice.
text_fidelity_b: Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel

A Mustard Seed Toys Tungsten Putty Weight, 1 oz, Get The Perfect Weights for Your Pinewood Car to Win Your Derby I've been working on pinewood derby cars for a while. I first started with my children, then the past 10 years holding derby car clinics.

Tungsten putty is important to get your car to maximum weight. I keep the unassembled car weighted at 4.9 ounces. I drill a shallow 1/4 hole under the car and pack in the tungsten putty to make up the last bit of weight. That way on race day you can make small weight adjustments without trashing your car. The fastest car is the heaviest.

I've been getting tungsten putty from the large online derby suppliers. I figured I'd save money in shipping, use Amazon prime, and try a new product. This putty is less dense than the putty I've worked with in the past. It seems to have more sticky binder and less tungsten powder than what I've used in the past. I ordered 3 units. They easily fit inside one container. I even mixed some tungsten powder to the 3 blobs of putty.

I prefer the stuff I got before but this will work

Igloo Ice Cube, Ocean Blue, 14-can Capacity, 32607 ORIGINAL REVIEW: I replaced my previous Igloo cooler with this one and I really like it. The top compartment is handy. The previous igloo cooler was a bit smaller and was bought in 1992. It still works great except the handle wont stay on so it was time for a new one. I mention this because it's 24 years old and still works. that says a lot for igloo quality. I hope to get that kind of service from this cooler. The only reason the handle failed was because I stumbled and sent the cooler flying. If that had not have happened I probably would not have needed to buy this one. Igloo is rugged, last a long time and with 2 ice packs about the same size as the sides of this cooler, everything stays cool for at least 24 hours as long as it's not in direct sunlight. I'm not one for change, especially when I have a product that works and lasts. I really did need a little larger cooler so yes, I miss the old cooler but not so much because I really like this new one much better. I donated the old one and found it good home. Yes I know it's just a cooler but I used t every work day for 24 years, I got a little attached to it. They still make that model and I nearly bought it but my wife found this new one. Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black) NGL, it's a slick looking knife, but it isn't well constructed.

The blade looks good and the scales feel good in the hand. The blade definitely is sharp. The issue is the pivot point of the knife and the scales around the pivot point.

You'll notice that there is a nice index finger groove up near the pivot point. This is a nice ergo component, however when gripping the knife here the scales flex and cause a severe amount of blade play at the pivot point. Inversely, grabbing the blade towards the base and wigging it will cause the scales at that finger well to flex.

As much as I would like to write this off as a 1-off construction issue, I had an unrelated individual talk about the very same issue they had with this knife. They had sourced the knife from their local B&M and had mentioned the issue. I told them I had one in the mail and would check it when the knife showed up. Sure enough 2 instances of this knife with the same issue.

So buyer beware. I have heard good things about this knife maker and this knife so I decided to test the waters with this blade. I will be sending this knife back and I doubt I will be buying another Eafengrow even if it's another G-10 D2 for sub $20.
text_fidelity_b: Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Sea Eagle 3 Person Inflatable Portable Sport Kayak Canoe w/Paddles Purchased this boat directly from Sea Eagle. They offered a 180 day risk free trial. Returned it after 2 1/2 weeks and they accepted my return for a full refund, no questions asked. A very smooth transaction. Would definitely deal with them again.

The 370 hull is 32lbs, not 26 as in Amazon's description. They confused the 330 and the 370.

As a 5'2" woman, I found that I couldn't manage all the transport and packing of this 12 1/2 ft long boat comfortably on my own. Even with the help of a friend, we had a difficult time repacking everything. And we never did get it back in the carry bag. 32lbs of a solid object is easier to handle than 32lbs of 12 1/2 ft long deflated rubber.

And keep in mind that if you are buying this because you live in an apartment or condo and lack outside storage space, you'll need to rinse and hand dry the boat each time you use it before rolling and repacking it.

Having said that, the boat is sturdy and stable when inflated and I never felt ''tippy" in it.

Of course any inflatable takes more paddling effort than a hardshell and that needs to be considered too. But the paddles provided were fairly lightweight and easy to handle.

Tracking was just okay.

IMHO this makes a good vacation kayak. But wouldn't want to deal with extra maintenance and packing on a regular basis.
text_fidelity_b: Sea Eagle 3 Person Inflatable Portable Sport Kayak Canoe w/Paddles

text_fidelity_a:
Avenir Dual Action Bell Talk about a good value. You can easily spend more, but I doubt you'd get a much better sounding bell. The Avenir Dual Action Bell has that instantly recognizable brrrriiiinngg sound that gently alerts people ahead that a bicycle is approaching.

It's not too loud and it's not too soft, it's just the right volume, and you can easily control the length of the brriiiinnggg, making it short or long. I have mine mounted on the left side, which lets me easily push the lever forward with my thumb. Again, the lever action is not too stiff or too loose, it's just right, allowing quick multiple rings if you like, but also giving excellent control for just a quick short half ring if that's what you prefer.

Quality seems quite high for such an inexpensive item. The attachment clamp (plastic) is nice in that it will close around small handlebars or larger size bars with it's long bolt. One point, be sure and watch out for the little screw at the top of the clamp (where the bolt screws into), as it can easily fall out and go missing while doing the attachment. It's VERY small and took me awhile to find, as it bounced quite a distance. All it takes is keeping your fingers on each side during the attachment process, not a big deal as long you know to do it.

Highly recommended for those who enjoy not only the wonderful sound of a traditional bicycle bell, but also getting a good value as well.
text_fidelity_b: Avenir Dual Action Bell

text_fidelity_a: Gazelle Supreme Glider Cardio Home Fitness Training Exercise Machine with Hydraulic Resistance w/ Grip Pulse Technology Water Bottle Holder & 3 DVDs I Highly Recommend watching the assembly video on YouTube. When they assembled this part, they had the bearing cocked and not set in the key slot. I called the 1-800 number and they sent me a new cable assembly with the hardware. I couldn't get the screw out of the bottom of the cable. The cheap allen wrench stripped the screw. I used my dremel with a cut-off wheel to cut a slot in the screw for a screw driver. I installed the new cable assembly and everything is working fine. No squeaking and grinding. I purchased a small tube of lithium grease at the auto parts store before assembly. I put enough grease on everything to last two lifetimes. The grease that was on it was a thin coating of tacky something. My Gazelle glides smoothly and quietly. It was worth the extra time to grease everything when I assembled it. I didn't see the need for a water bottle so I cut off the top third and use it to hold my tv remote. The Dvds are terrible! text_fidelity_a: Babolat Pure Drive (6-Pack) Tennis Bag (Blue) This RH6 Pure bag has five major pockets, (two major top ones, one side, one smaller semi-rigid side and one underneath vented pocket for shoe/towel/sweatbands/etc).with mini-pockets within those pockets for order. Similar bags only seemed to have 3-4 pockets  The semi-rigid pocket holds its shape and may(?) help protect items such as a phone. The shoe pocket has a small circle vent which doesn't look like it will do much but most other bags have no vent at all. I liked my (very) old Prince bag which had several mesh pockets for breathing but no one seems to make those anymore. This has more volume than the Prince bag which tapered mostly straight down while this one curves down more at the end. The top thermal pocket which can hold 3 rackets. while the other top pocket is not thermal but is much larger. For giggles, I was able to get seven rackets in the second pocket. Backpack straps on top rather than a single shoulder strap, a matter of preference, plus a top handle and end handle. This fits my needs very well (except for the lack of ventilation) because I like to keep different things (balls/water; towels/sweat bands; supports/braces/medical kit; keys/phone/wallet; etc) in different pockets rather than rutting around in one big pocket as I captain a small group on five courts.
